entities.summary: William Montagu, 1st Earl of Salisbury, was a pivotal figure in 14th-century English politics and military affairs. A loyal servant of King Edward III, Montagu played a key role in the Hundred Years' War against France. He was instrumental in the Battle of Crécy (1346) and the Battle of Poitiers (1356), where English forces defeated the French, securing a crucial victory for the English monarchy. Montagu's military successes and strategic alliances with other nobles helped solidify English dominance in the region. His legacy extended beyond his military achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Black Death relief efforts. Montagu's impact on English history can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Lancastrian dynasty, which ruled England from 1399 to 1471. The Earl's reputation as a skilled military leader and statesman has endured for centuries, making him one of the most notable figures of the medieval period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Montagu's military successes and strategic alliances played a significant role in shaping English dominance in the region, while his legacy extended beyond his military achievements to include patronage of the arts and support for relief efforts during the Black Death pandemic.
